title: Adaptive league all-policy-heads pilot
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: All-street league PPO on the dedicated preflop and postflop policy heads, under exact-source KL with a frozen shared representation, will address the preflop axis left untouched by postflop-only pilots while avoiding full-trunk representation drift.
material_change: Add --all-policy-heads-only-training; resume Standard10; train policy_head, preflop_policy_head and value_head only; all-street PPO; source KL 1; target KL 0.01; advantage clip 3; lr 3e-5; same adaptive three-opponent league and 25% self-play.
baseline: Postflop-head predecessor completed 263464 hands and later checkpoints had positive point estimates against all three internal anchors, but iter48 confirmation lower bounds remained negative vs Standard10 and CFR96; no Slumbot promotion.

result.summary: All-policy-heads all-street league training completed 263602 production hands with exact frozen-trunk scope and stable trust-region metrics. Iter32 maximized direction-consistent three-anchor discovery mean, but untouched confirmation lower bounds remained negative versus Standard10 and corrected CFR96; no Slumbot run was launched.
result.conclusion: Training both dedicated policy heads broadened changed decisions and strongly beat the Slumbot-free anchor, but head-only capacity did not establish robust improvement over the source Standard10 or CFR96. The evidence does not support scaling this head-only lineage further.
result.next_step: Test genuine full-network all-street representation learning at one-tenth the head-only learning rate with stronger source KL and tighter target KL; smoke-test trust-region and preflop behavior before a bounded pilot.
